newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge release French bikers after one day.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge release French bikers after one day.

text.p: Khmer Rouge defectors on Monday released three French motorcyclists a day after seizing them in central Cambodia, diplomatic and government officials said.
Interior Ministry Secretary of State Ho Sok told Reuters the three had driven to an isolated village about 90 km (55 miles) northwest of Phnom Penh.
The official said Khmer Rouge defectors from division 919, which broke away earlier this month from hardliners loyal to Pol Pot, stopped and held the three when they neared their base.
"We and a French diplomat went to the scene and discussed the matter with them yesterday evening and everything was solved the same day," Ho Sok said.

"It is true that three French people have been abducted (on Sunday) and liberated today," a French diplomat said, adding that the three had not been harmed and had returned to Phnom Penh from Kompong Chhnang province, where they were seized.
The envoy would not identify the three locally employed Frenchmen and did not know if they had been robbed.
The Khmer Rouge have been fighting the royal coalition government formed after U.N.-run polls in 1993, which the guerrillas rejected after reneging on a 1991 peace treaty.

But the Maoist movement, responsible for the deaths of more than one million people during Pol Pot's 1975-79 rule, has suffered a series of recent setbacks with a split in August with former top cadre Ieng Sary and several further defections this month.
Since resuming their armed struggle in 1993, the guerrillas have killed at least seven foreigners and abducted several more.

Breakaway Khmer Rouge commander Chea Bunheng told reporters on Sunday that British mine clearance specialist Christopher Howes was alive and well seven months after being kidnapped and taken to the hardliners' northern base at Anlong Veng.
